title: Stop the booking form from creating impossible bookings

blocks.text: The meeting-room calendar has bookings that end before they start, and a few with no organiser, so nobody can be asked to free the room. They all came from the booking form, which creates a `Booking` through `Booking.builder()`: it calls a setter every time the user fills in or changes a field, in whatever order the user goes, and calls `build()` when the user presses Save.

Finish `build()` in `src/main/java/practice/Booking.java`. Every booking needs a room, an organiser, a start and an end, and must end after it starts. Refuse any other with `Booking.InvalidBooking`, whose message the form shows next to the fields; a booking that can take place is created as the user left it. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a booking with a room, an organiser and a start before its end is created with those values
a valid booking is created whatever order its fields were filled in
a booking that ends before it starts is refused even when its end was filled in before its start
a booking that ends at the moment it starts is refused
a booking with no organiser is refused with InvalidBooking, which the form can show
a booking whose times were changed on the way is judged by the times it ends up with

origin.section: A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set

concepts: A builder checks rules that relate parts, and required parts, in build(), so the result does not depend on the order the setters were called in or on intermediate states.
